symptom: The research-only shadow mapper validated caller-owned source row fields and later reread the same object for sourceRowDigest and ledger record construction. A synthetic accessor can return different current_odds values across reads; a Proxy get trap can disagree with its own-data descriptor. A Node 22.16.0 synthetic two-read reproduction showed validated 6.4 versus recorded 7.1. This is a source-row consistency failure, not a production incident or external evidence claim.
lesson: Validating an untrusted row is not sufficient when the same caller-owned object is read again for digest and output fields. Accessors and Proxy get hooks can make the audited value differ from the validated value without any SHA-256 collision.
guardrail: Capture every allowlisted source field once through enumerable own data descriptors into a detached null-prototype snapshot before shape/PIT validation, digesting or ledger mapping. Reject accessors, missing fields and throwing descriptor traps without invoking source getters. Regress accessor rejection and Proxy get/descriptor disagreement while retaining baseline valid digests. This does not authenticate sources or authorize production.
